Subject: Admin activity export: timezone-normalized indices & retention carve-outs

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this—Novomed is preparing our SOC 2 evidence bundle and we need clarity on the admin activity exports Redwood can provide. Specifically:

- What fields are captured in the admin activity ledger (examples: user_id, action, resource, ip, timestamp, request_id, session_id, role) — any info about operator role mapping would help.
- Can timestamps be normalized to a named timezone (we want America/New_York for our ops team) while also providing UTC epoch?
- Retention windows: what default retention for admin activity, and can you carve out shorter/longer windows per account?
- Export modes & SLA: on-demand sample export, near-real-time streaming vs bulk snapshot; delivery mechanisms (S3 presigned, SFTP, signed manifests).
- Evidence integrity: checksums/HMACs, signed manifests, and proof-of-delivery options for chain-of-custody.

Can you provide a small 7-day sample (timezone normalized to EST) and a manifest we can use for checksum verification? We also need an estimate for a monthly export (30 days) SLA and redaction options for PII.

If possible, please share a schema and a short matrix of export options. Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps—our security lead (CC'd) may join.

Thanks,
Jorge Ramirez
Senior IT Audit Manager
Novomed Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Admin activity export: timezone-normalized indices & retention carve-outs

Hi Jorge — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I've attached a concise schema and an export-options matrix for reference.

What we log (admin activity ledger, non-exhaustive):
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601), timezone_offset (minutes), user_id, operator_role, action_type, target_resource (type/id), request_id, session_id, source_ip, user_agent, kv_cache_hit, cache_ops, bytes_in, bytes_out, trace_id

Timezone normalization:
- We provide the raw UTC timestamp and an optional normalized_timestamp field set to the named timezone you request (e.g., America/New_York). Normalization is done at export time and included in CSV/Parquet exports.

Retention & carve-outs:
- Default retention for admin activity: 365 days.
- We support configurable retention per account: 90/180/365/indefinite (legal-hold) with export-only short-term windows available. Legal holds can freeze deletion for specific timeboxes.

Export modes & delivery SLA:
- On-demand sample (<= 7 days): S3 presigned, SFTP, or direct Drive link; typical SLA 48 hours.
- Bulk monthly export (<= 30 days): delivery within 5 business days for non-sensitive exports; redacted exports may take up to 7 business days depending on scope.
- Streaming: audit stream available to customers via secure webhook or Kafka mirror (requires onboarding).

Evidence integrity:
- Every export comes with a signed manifest (HMAC-SHA256) and per-file SHA256 checksums. For legal-hold handoffs we also provide signed attestation PDF.

Redaction & sampling:
- We support column-level redaction (PII hashing), row-level sampling, and per-tenant redaction rules. Please specify which identifier fields you want redacted.

Next steps / proposed call:
- I can produce a 7-day timezone-normalized sample (America/New_York) and deliver via S3 presigned link with signed manifest.
- Please confirm the exact start/end dates, whether you want operator role mapping included, and any redaction flags.
- Proposal: 30-min call tomorrow (Thu 22 May) at 15:00 ET to walk through the manifest and delivery.

Attachments: admin_activity_schema_v1.csv, export_options_matrix.pdf

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Hi Jorge — Ben from Infra here, adding technical delivery details and the request checklist.

Delivery options we can support now:
- S3 presigned PUT (preferred for large files) or presigned GET for delivery; files encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys if requested.
- Secure SFTP (username/key) for partners that require SFTP ingress.
- Encrypted tarball + signed manifest (.manifest.txt) containing SHA256 sums for every file. The manifest itself is HMAC-SHA256 signed with our export key; we can rotate keys and provide public verification keys on request.

Manifest & integrity example (we'll provide this format):
- manifest: sample_manifest_stub.txt (attached) — shows file list, SHA256, compressed_size, and HMAC signature line.

Request checklist for an on-demand sample:
1) Account ID / Org: Novomed Health (please confirm).
2) Start / End timestamps (ISO).
3) Timezone for normalization (e.g., America/New_York).
4) Delivery method (S3 presigned URL OR SFTP).
5) Redaction flags (columns to mask/hash).
6) Include operator role map? (yes/no) — if yes, provide mapping format (we map internal role ids to display names).

SLA estimates (small exports):
- 0-7 day sample: ~48 hours after complete request + verification.
- 8-30 day export: 3-5 business days.
- >30 day or cross-region exports: 5-10 business days depending on redaction complexity.

Legal hold & chain of custody:
- If you request a legal hold freeze, we provide a signed attestation and mark the dataset as preserved; deletions will be blocked per account policy.

Action items (from our side):
- Hannah: produce schema + export options (done, attached).
- Ben: stage a sample job and provide presigned URL after confirmation of timebox.
- Marissa: coordinate any billing or transfer approvals if customer requests indefinite retention.

Attachments: sample_manifest_stub.txt

Thanks — ready when you are.

Ben Carter
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
